note: Acquisition routes: where a registered source's public bytes live, what the cycle and lead grammars are, and how the fetched objects compose into the primary/supplement/donor roles the packaged decode profile binds. This document is DATA. Adding a model's front door is a row here, not a code path; gpuwm/fetch_routes.py is the one engine that reads every row. Every host, path template and ladder below was measured against the live service on the date in `measured`.
endpoint_note: Every source's hosts are an ORDERED LADDER, not a set. The router resolves the concrete cycle first, then takes the entries whose `retention_hours` covers that cycle's age -- so a cycle older than the operational window goes straight to the archive instead of paying for a doomed attempt. `retention_hours: null` is an archive: effectively unbounded. When NO entry covers the age the whole ladder is still tried, because retention is an optimisation and not a bar. Failure -- a refused connection, 403/503, a Retry-After the host's own retry discipline could not wait out, or a payload that does not verify -- moves to the next entry; when every entry fails the refusal names each one and why. Each retention figure below was measured by counting the day directories the live tree served on the date named in its `why`.
transfer_note: `transfer_rank` is a SECOND order over the same rungs, and it decides which host moves the bytes rather than which hosts are asked. Lower is quicker; absent means the ladder position, so a source that declares no rank transfers in table order and nothing about it changes. The two orders differ for exactly one reason: the operational server's advantage is having a cycle FIRST, and that advantage is spent the moment the archive has the same object -- after which what is left is throughput, which the archive wins. Measured at peak hours, the operational server paced whole-file transfers at about 3 MB/s per file, so a 3.4 GB request took about 20 minutes where the archive served the same volume in about 3. So for each requested object inside the retention window the engine asks the throughput rung whether it HAS that object (one HEAD, milliseconds against a multi-hundred-megabyte transfer) and promotes it when it does. Promotion REORDERS the ladder and never shortens it: every rung stays behind the chosen one, fall-through and the whole-ladder refusal are unchanged, and a probe that 404s or errors costs the transfer nothing.

nomads.ncep.noaa.gov.why: NCEP's operational server is one shared public service behind Akamai and it answers an aggressive client with an over-rate-limit page and then an IP block. Two is deliberate rather than small-for-safety's-sake: the node-wide governor already spaces request STARTS 2.5 s apart, and the service answers in about 3.1 s, so a second in-flight request is exactly enough to keep the pipeline full. A third would only queue on the governor while holding another connection open against a service that throttles.

legacy_ladders.note: The three sources whose transport predates this table (gfs, gdas, hrrr) still declare their endpoints HERE, in the same row shape as a route's `hosts`, so preferring the operational server is one table fact for every NCEP source rather than two mechanisms. Their host vocabulary is their own -- `s3` where the table routes say `aws` -- because that is the name their --transport has accepted since before the table existed.

aigfs.host_note: NOMADS ONLY, and the refusal to mirror is deliberate. noaa-nws-graphcastgfs-pds publishes objects under byte-identical key names that are a DIFFERENT product -- the experimental EAGLE stream, subCentre 2 against the operational subCentre 0, 65 pres messages against 78, and 500 hPa geopotential height differing by 8.7 gpm. Every packaged selector pins subcenter=0, so the S3 copies refuse at decode by identity octet. Nothing in the filename distinguishes them. SCN 25-89: 'Data for these models will be on the NCEP NOMADS server only'. NOMADS keeps a 10-day rolling window; there is no archive behind this door.

donors.why: AIGFS publishes no soil, no land mask, no orography, no skin temperature, no surface pressure and no 2 m humidity. The packaged profile aigfs-gdas-hybrid-grib2-v1 binds the land-surface canonicals to the SAME-CYCLE GDAS analysis and derives surface pressure at every lead from AIGFS's own mean-sea-level pressure at the analysis terrain height; a donor from another cycle or grid refuses by name. Without the donor `gpuwm prep --source aigfs` refuses at init naming the missing surfaces.

record_subset.why: there is no NOMADS grib-filter CGI for aigfs (filter_aigfs.pl is a 404) -- whole-file transfer is the only route the service offers

compose.name: composed/gdps_{YYYYMMDDHH}_PT{FFF}H.grib2
compose.why: GDPS ships one message per file; a valid time is that lead's files concatenated, which is the standard GRIB2 multi-record form. Orography, land mask and the ice analysis exist ONLY at the analysis lead, and the profile declares them once-per-cycle invariants the engine broadcasts, so they join the first composed state and nothing else.

record_subset.why: each Datamart object is ONE GRIB2 message -- the file IS the record

20crv3.why: the 20CRv3 every-member GRIB2 archive is not published on an anonymously readable public endpoint; only the ensemble-MEAN NetCDF distribution is, and a member state is not a mean.
20crv3.remedy: bring the member's files yourself into DIR; `gpuwm prep --source 20crv3 --source-root DIR --author-only --author-input-manifest DIR/member-manifest.json` writes the member manifest and prints the --source-manifest pair a standalone `gpuwm prep --source 20crv3` binds, and `gpuwm go CONFIG.toml --data-dir DIR` runs the whole chain from a `gpuwm domain --source 20crv3` config.

20crv3-cf.why: the NOAA PSL 20CRv3 NetCDF distribution is a per-year, per-variable reanalysis archive with no cycle and no forecast lead, so --cycle/--hours describe nothing in it. It is also missing orography and a land mask entirely, which the packaged profile recovers with tools/build_pressure_level_invariant_supplement.py from files you already hold.

source_root.why: the folder tools/download_20crv3_native_subset.py writes: one NetCDF file per variable, plus invariant.nc, the orography and land mask it recovers from them.

supplements.why: the recovered orography and land mask: an input like every other file, and the terrain supplement the composition binds by this role. wilt.nc is only what it was recovered from, so it is not an input.

mapped.why: `mapped` is the generic declarative adapter, not a product: it names no publisher, no bucket and no file grammar, so there is nothing for a fetch to resolve. It is the door for bytes you already have.
mapped.remedy: supply the mapping and composition documents beside the files: `gpuwm prep --source mapped --source-format FORMAT --mapping MAPPING.json --composition COMPOSITION.json --provenance ROLE=PROVENANCE.json --input FILE --supplement ROLE=FILE --author-input-manifest inputs.json --experiment-config CONFIG.toml --wps-namelist CONFIG.namelist.wps --geog-root WPS_GEOG --output-root PREPARED`.

era5-l137.why: ERA5 model-level data is served by the Copernicus Climate Data Store as a queued MARS request (dataset reanalysis-era5-complete, levtype=ml, levelist=1/to/137), not as files at a predictable URL: there is no cycle-and-lead path for a fetch to resolve, and the request runs under your own CDS account. The pressure-level/single-level analysis this source borrows its land surface from does have a fetch door, `gpuwm fetch --source era5 --retrieve`, which writes it into the same folder.

source_root.why: one folder holding the model-level file(s) from your MARS request and the same hours' surface analysis `gpuwm fetch --source era5 --retrieve --out` writes beside them.

supplements.why: the same hours' ERA5 pressure-level/single-level analysis the model-level atmosphere borrows its land surface, soil and lake state from; `gpuwm fetch --source era5 --retrieve` writes it under this name.

request.keywords: class=ea expver=1 stream=oper type=an levtype=ml levelist=1/to/137 param=130/131/132/133 grid=0.25/0.25 format=grib
request.why: the model-level atmosphere, requested for the same hours and over the lattice points the surface analysis delivers for the same area -- its corners taken inward onto the 0.25 degree lattice, as the provider does for that fetch -- so the two grids share their points.
